title: Topology enables learning-based hydrodynamic prediction of the global river system
abstract: arXiv:2602.22293v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Accurate river prediction is essential for water, food and energy security, yet remains challenging across entire river networks. Machine learning has transformed Earth-system modeling, but a system-level advance for river prediction lags for lack of reliable data. Exploiting the connectivity and dissipative dynamics of rivers, we introduce GraphRiverCast, a neural model for global river systems that predicts daily multivariate hydrodynamics at every reach of a 0.25{\deg}network with only sparse gauges and no initial state. It shows no intrinsic skill decay with lead time, outperforms leading global river models by 25% in accuracy, and robustly generalizes to ungauged reaches and finer resolutions. GraphRiverCast lifts learning-based river prediction from isolated basins to a unified global system and offers insights for machine learning in data-scarce Earth systems.

translated_title: 拓扑结构赋能全球河系基于学习的水动力预测
translated_abstract: 准确的河流预测对于水、粮食和能源安全至关重要，但在整个河网中仍具挑战性。机器学习已变革了地球系统建模，但河系预测的系统级进展因缺乏可靠数据而滞后。利用河流的连通性和耗散动力学，我们引入了GraphRiverCast，这是一个针对全球河系的神经模型，能在0.25度网络的每个河段预测每日多元水动力，仅依赖稀疏的测量站且无需初始状态。该模型在预测时效上无内在技能衰减，在准确性上比领先的全球河流模型高出25%，并能稳健地泛化至未测量的河段和更精细的分辨率。GraphRiverCast将基于学习的河流预测从孤立流域提升为统一的全球系统，并为数据稀缺的地球系统中的机器学习提供了见解。
tldr: 本文提出GraphRiverCast，利用河流拓扑结构实现全球河系的每日水动力预测，无需初始状态，精度提升25%并泛化至未测量区域。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces GraphRiverCast, a topology-aware neural model for global river systems that predicts daily hydrodynamics without initial states, achieving 25% higher accuracy and robust generalization to ungauged reaches.
